inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, authenticated via SSO

instructions.note: Prompt grants the agent authority to act using the engineer's own credentials for production deploy and migration actions, with no independent scoping or review, implicitly extending the engineer's full authority to the agent for irreversible actions.
Prompt explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation before acting, removing any possibility of human-in-the-loop review immediately prior to irreversible production actions.

controls.name: SSO authentication gate restricting access to on-call engineers
Cloud audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging occurs independent of model behavior, but it attributes every action to the engineer's identity and does not record the agent's reasoning or original request, so it has limited forensic value for distinguishing agent-directed from human-directed action.

controls.name: Human approval gate for production deploy/migration (recommended)
Immutable, non-deletable record of request and agent justification tied to a distinct agent-actor identity (recommended)

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executed with engineer's broad personal credential and no approval gate

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor for changes to cloud audit log retention/access policy, or any widening of the engineer's token scope or self-service deletion rights.

evidence.observation: Agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token to perform production actions; the token is passed in at session start with no stated scope limitation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, confirming irreversibility of cap.db_migrate.
System prompt instructs the agent to run migrations in production directly using the engineer's credentials and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Add a mandatory human approval gate with raw_action review (showing the exact migration target and script) before any production database migration executes.
Replace use of the engineer's personal broad-scope access token with a least-privilege, action-scoped service credential limited to migration execution.
Record an immutable copy of the request and the agent's stated justification, tied to a distinguishable agent-actor identity, alongside each cloud audit log entry for this capability.

findings.title: Production deployment executed with engineer's broad personal credential and no approval gate

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor for changes to cloud audit log retention/access policy, or any widening of the engineer's token scope or self-service deletion rights.

evidence.observation: Agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token to perform production actions; the token is passed in at session start with no stated scope limitation.
System prompt instructs the agent to deploy the named service in production using the engineer's credentials and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Add a mandatory human approval gate with raw_action review (showing the exact service and target environment) before any production deployment executes.
Replace use of the engineer's personal broad-scope access token with a least-privilege, action-scoped deploy-only service credential.
Record an immutable copy of the request and the agent's stated justification, tied to a distinguishable agent-actor identity, alongside each cloud audit log entry for this capability.

findings.title: Shared identity logging plus engineer-deletable chat history defeats attribution of agent-directed production actions

attack_path.note: Action executed under the engineer's identity via their credential.
Action executed under the engineer's identity via their credential.
Records only that the engineer performed the action; does not distinguish agent-initiated from human-initiated action.
The only record of what was requested and why; deletable at will by the same engineer whose identity the action is logged under.

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor whether engineer self-service deletion rights extend to the cloud audit log, or whether audit log retention/access controls are weakened, which would remove the last intact record entirely.

evidence.observation: The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not under any distinct agent-actor identity.

recommendations.action: Capture the chat request and the agent's generated justification in a separate, immutable (write-once) log correlated to each production action, independent of the user-deletable chat history.

Tag each production action in the cloud audit log with a distinct agent-actor identity, separate from the human identity, to preserve non-repudiation between human-directed and model-initiated actions.
Restrict or disable engineers' ability to delete chat history that documents requests leading to irreversible production actions.

rating.rationale: Trusted, SSO-authenticated on-call engineers can direct irreversible production database migrations and production deployments using the engineer's own broad personal access token. No approval gate exists for either action, the prompt explicitly forbids seeking confirmation, and autonomy has no step or runtime limit, so the autonomy modifier applies to both S3 sinks, raising inherent risk from the base moderate (trusted source, severe sink) to high. No preventive, approval, or credential-scoping control exists in the design, so residual risk does not improve on inherent risk for either capability. A third, cross-cutting finding addresses repudiation: the cloud audit log attributes every production action solely to the engineer's identity rather than a distinct agent actor, and the only record of what was requested and why (the chat transcript) is deletable by that same engineer, defeating non-repudiation for both the irreversible migration and the deployment. Forecast stays at the same tier across all findings because the only credited control throughout is detective audit logging, which carries no tier credit under the rubric; its removal would further erode accountability without itself changing the computed tier. Confidence is high because every material fact driving these findings (shared broad credential, no rollback for migrations, explicit removal of confirmation, deletable chat history, identity-only audit attribution) is explicitly stated in the provided artifacts.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, IaC, or token policy was provided; the exact scope of the engineer's personal access token is inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified, so confidence on precise privilege boundaries is somewhat limited despite being rated high based on the explicit text.
No information was given on deploy rollback mechanics beyond general assumption; the partially_reversible classification for cap.prod_deploy is inferred, not confirmed by the artifacts.
